title: Road Hazard Protection Coverage Expiration
content:
Road Hazard Protection coverage ends on its own; the holder does nothing.

- The certificate must be in status active when it expires.
- It expires on the day after its expiration date, or earlier on the date the covered tire set closes as worn out or retired, because the tires it covers are no longer in service.
- A covered set closed as returned does not expire the certificate; the certificate is cancelled with a covered-set-returned refund instead.
- Unused roadside calls and unused repairs or replacements lapse at expiry without any refund.

| Event on the covered set or certificate | Effect on the certificate |
|---|---|
| expiration date passes | expires on the day after the expiration date |
| set closed as worn out | expires on the closing date |
| set closed as retired | expires on the closing date |
| set closed as returned | does not expire; cancelled with a covered-set-returned refund |

*Hypothetical example.* A certificate with an expiration date of June 30 and an active set expires on July 1. If the set had been closed as worn out on April 12, the certificate would have expired on April 12. In either case its two unused roadside calls lapse with no refund.
